title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events — what you did, where you were, what happened — using the simple past, perfect and past continuous.
intro: The Odia past tense is refreshingly regular: add **-ଇଲି** for 'I', **-ଇଲା** for 'he/she', **-ଇଲେ** for respectful and plural subjects. If you know Hindi, there is a nice surprise: Odia has **no ergative construction** — the subject stays the subject and the verb agrees with it, even with transitive verbs (ମୁଁ ଭାତ ଖାଇଲି, not *mujh-ne*…).

vocab.note: ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ 'last week', ଗତ ବର୍ଷ 'last year'.
ମୋର ଜନ୍ମ କଟକରେ 'I was born in Cuttack'.
ମୁଁ ଥିଲି, ତୁମେ ଥିଲ, ଆପଣ ଥିଲେ, ସେ ଥିଲା.

vocab.en: to be found, be available; to get

phrases.en: Have you eaten? (a common friendly greeting)

grammar.title: Simple past: -ଇଲି, -ଇଲା, -ଇଲେ (no ergative!)
grammar.body:
Add the past endings to the stem:
ମୁଁ ଦେଖିଲି *dekhili* — I saw
ଆମେ / ତୁ ଦେଖିଲୁ *dekhilu* — we / you (intimate) saw
ତୁମେ ଦେଖିଲ *dekhilô* — you (familiar) saw
ଆପଣ ଦେଖିଲେ *dekhile* — you (formal) saw
ସେ ଦେଖିଲା *dekhila* — he/she saw
ସେ / ସେମାନେ ଦେଖିଲେ *dekhile* — he/she (respectful) / they saw

**Irregular**: କରିବା → **କଲି, କଲା, କଲେ**; ଯିବା → **ଗଲି, ଗଲା, ଗଲେ**; ଦେବା → **ଦେଲି**; ନେବା → **ନେଲି**; ହେବା → **ହେଲି, ହେଲା**; ଅଛି → **ଥିଲି, ଥିଲା, ଥିଲେ** 'was'.

**No ergative**: unlike Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi or Marathi, Odia keeps the subject in its normal form and the verb agrees with *it*, whether the verb is transitive or not: ମୁଁ ଚିଠି ଲେଖିଲି 'I wrote a letter' — compare Hindi *maiṃne ciṭṭhī likhī*.

**Negative**: 'didn't' is usually the -ଇ form + ନାହିଁ (ମୁଁ ଯାଇ ନାହିଁ 'I didn't go / haven't gone'); the past + ନାହିଁ (ମୁଁ ଗଲି ନାହିଁ) is also heard, especially for a deliberate 'didn't'.

examples.en: I haven't had breakfast. / I didn't have breakfast.

grammar.title: Perfect, past perfect and past continuous
grammar.body:
**Present perfect -ଇଛି** — recent or relevant now: ମୁଁ ଖାଇଛି 'I have eaten', ସେ ଆସିଛନ୍ତି 'he/she has come'. Very common in conversation, often where English uses a simple past.

**Past perfect -ଇଥିଲି** — 'had done', also used for events in the more distant past: ମୁଁ ଗତ ବର୍ଷ କୋଣାର୍କ ଯାଇଥିଲି 'I went to Konark last year'.

**Past continuous -ଉଥିଲି** — 'was doing': ମୁଁ ପଢ଼ୁଥିଲି 'I was studying'; also 'used to': ପିଲାଦିନେ ମୁଁ ପୋଖରୀରେ ପହଁରୁଥିଲି 'as a child I used to swim in the pond'.

All take the usual person endings: -ଥିଲି, -ଥିଲୁ, -ଥିଲ, -ଥିଲେ, -ଥିଲା.

examples.en: I went to Konark last year.
At that time I was studying.

dialogue.title: A trip to Konark
dialogue.setting: On Monday, Lipi asks Sam about his weekend.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: Sam, what did you do on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କ ସହ କୋଣାର୍କ ଗଲି।
lines.roman: muṃ mo saṅgômanôṅkô sôhô Koṇarkô gôli.
lines.en: I went to Konark with my friends.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ! ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟ ମନ୍ଦିରର ଚକଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଦେଖି ମୁଁ ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟ ହୋଇଗଲି।
lines.roman: ôdbhutô! Surjyô Môndirôrô chôkôguṛikô dekhi muṃ aschôrjyô hoigôli.
lines.en: Amazing! I was astonished when I saw the wheels of the Sun Temple.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: Did you go to Chandrabhaga beach?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେଠି ଗୋଟିଏ ଘଟଣା ଘଟିଲା।
lines.roman: hôṃ, kintu seṭhi goṭie ghôṭôṇa ghôṭila.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୋ ଚପଲ ବାଲିରେ ହଜିଗଲା! ମୁଁ ଖାଲି ପାଦରେ ବସ୍ ଷ୍ଟାଣ୍ଡ ଯାଏ ଚାଲିଲି।
lines.roman: mo chôpôlô balire hôjigôla! muṃ khali padôre bôs sṭaṇḍ jae chalili.
lines.en: My sandals got lost in the sand! I walked barefoot all the way to the bus stand.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଶେଷରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଦୋକାନରୁ ନୂଆ ଚପଲ କିଣିଲି, ଆଉ ରାତି ଦଶଟାରେ ଘରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲି।
lines.roman: sesôre goṭie dokanôru nua chôpôlô kiṇili, au rati dôsôṭare ghôre pôhôñchili.
lines.en: In the end I bought new sandals at a shop and got home at ten at night.

culture: The 13th-century **Sun Temple at Konark** (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) is built as the Sun God's chariot, with 24 carved stone wheels that work as sundials; its wheel appears on Indian banknotes. Odisha's 'golden triangle' for visitors is Bhubaneswar (the 'temple city'), Puri and Konark.
